newsitem.title: USA: South Carolina House approves road bond bank.
newsitem.headline: South Carolina House approves road bond bank.

text.p: South Carolina's House of Representatives approved the creation of a $1.3 billion infrastructure bank to issue bonds for road construction in fast-growing urban and tourist areas.
The proposal passed 83-37 Wednesday despite complaints from lawmakers who said rural areas were shortchanged.
It would allow the state to transfer up to $97 million of gasoline tax revenues into the infrastucture bank annually to pay debt service on road construction bonds.
The revenue would include one cent of the state gas tax that now goes into the general fund, and up to 10 percent of the state's share of federal gasoline tax revenues.
Projects funded by the bonds would be selected by the legislature's 10-member Jonet Bond Reveiw Committee, with input from local governments.
The plan was expected to meet tough opposition in the Senate, whose leaders have alternately proposed raising the state's gasoline tax by up to 16 cents a gallon for pay-as-you-go road funding.
The proposal was proffered by Gov. David Beasley in his state-of-the state address. He opposes a gasoline tax increase but said he was confident a compromise could be worked out.
Critics said Beasley's plan could endanger South Carolina's bond rating.
"It's going to take away our AAA credit rating, which we have worked so mard to maintain," Rep. Ron Fleming, R-Union, told the Columbia State-Record.
